title: Rigveda 10.188: To Agni Jatavedas
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.188: To Agni Jatavedas: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.188 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to Agni Jatavedas. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 154r-154v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.188.1-3 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 46); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 154v
translation.original_text:
1pra nū̱naṁ jā̱tave̍dasa̱m aśva̍ṁ hinota vā̱jina̍m | i̱daṁ no̍ ba̱rhir ā̱sade̍ ||
2a̱sya pra jā̱tave̍daso̱ vipra̍vīrasya mī̱ḻhuṣa̍ḥ | ma̱hīm i̍yarmi suṣṭu̱tim ||
3yā ruco̍ jā̱tave̍daso deva̱trā ha̍vya̱vāha̍nīḥ | tābhi̍r no ya̱jñam i̍nvatu ||
translation.text:
1Now send ye Jâtavedas forth, send hitherward the vigorous Steed To seat him on our sacred grass.
2I raise the lofty eulogy of Jâtavedas, raining boons, With sages for his hero band.
3With flames of Jâtavedas which carry oblation to the Gods, May he promote our sacrifice.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 154v (OPenn image 154, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.188.1 ‹-jātavedasam aśvaṁ hinota vājinam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 155r, begins in RV 10.190.1 ‹-arṇavaḥ›. Verses 10.188.1-3 end on this page; 10.188.1 begins on fol. 154r.
